plan: My value is $40. In a first-round auction with no prior history, rational bidders will likely bid strategically near their value. My goal is to win without overpaying. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment, I want to bid just enough to win. Given the value range of $0-$49, a mid-range strategy around my value seems optimal. I'll bid slightly above my value to signal confidence but not so high that I risk significant loss.

With a private value of $13, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the winning strategy depends on predicting others' bids, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value. Other bidders likely have similar incentives. A bid around $11-$12 gives me a chance to win if others bid conservatively, while protecting against overpaying. The key is balancing potential gain against risk of losing the auction entirely.

My value is $17. In a first-price sealed bid auction with independent values, optimal strategy involves bidding strategically below my true value. Since others likely have random values between $0-$49, I'll aim to bid around my value but slightly under. A bid of $16 protects my potential profit margin while being competitive. I want to win if my value is higher than others, but avoid overpaying. The second-price mechanism means I only pay the next highest bid.
